Center]] |champion= |bowl= |bowl_result= }} {{2019–20 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2019–20 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Louisville]] during the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games on Denny Crum Court at the [[KFC Yum! Center]] in [[downtown Louisville|downtown Louisville, Kentucky]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They were led by second-year head coach [[Chris Mack (basketball)|Chris Mack]]. The Cardinals finished the season 24–7, and 15–5 in [[2019–20 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]]. The team was scheduled to play [[2019–20 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2020 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] before the tournament was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |title=Statement from ACC on Men's Basketball Tournament |url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/12/statement-from-acc-on-mens-basketball-tournament.aspx |website=theacc.com |publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference |access-date=12 March 2020}} The [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] was also cancelled due to the pandemic.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships|title=NCAA cancels remaining winter and spring championships}} ==Previous season== The [[2018–19 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Cardinals]] finished the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]] with a record of 20–14, 10–8 in [[2018–19 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], finishing in a tie for 6th place. They defeated [[2018–19 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]] in the second round of the [[2019 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] before losing to [[2018–19 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 7 seed, where they lost in the first round to [[2018–19 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]]. ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
